SR-001.justification: A SOCKS5 request for allowed.test\0.evil.test is refused (reply 2) with no query and no connection; ALLOWED.TEST. connects as allowed.test (an_allowed_host_is_reached_unchanged_over_both_protocols); the escape canaries r35_a_host_is_read_one_way refuse percent encoding and NUL through the real cage on macOS and T1; the host fuzz target (18.4 million inputs) found no host that is not a fixed point or that a resolver would read as an address.

SR-002.justification: With a domain-only list 2130706433, 0x7f.1, 017700000001, [::ffff:127.0.0.1], 127.1 and 127.0.0.1 are refused; with a range holding the address the decimal and dotted forms connect to the same echo host; no query is made.

SR-003.justification: Allowed names resolving to 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 and ::ffff:10.0.0.1 are refused with Reason::Address naming the address; the_checked_address_is_the_one_connected_to shows one query and a connect to the first checked address.

SR-004.justification: Three refused requests leave the counting resolver at zero queries.

SR-005.justification: An empty list returns AllowlistError::Empty; *, *.com, *.com:443, 0.0.0.0/0 and [::]/0 return TooWide; there is no constructor without entries.

SR-006.justification: On macOS a proxy-only child with no proxy listening fails both through the proxy and directly; on Linux a proxy-only cage without the proxy is refused, and with it the T1 namespace has no route but the listeners (r36 on escape_linux.rs); no code path connects directly.

SR-007.justification: On T1 direct TCP to a host port, ::1, a public address, UDP to a public resolver, TCP Fast Open, MPTCP, a raw socket and IPv6 all fail, and a datagram to the host loopback does not arrive; the macOS canary covers TCP, IPv6, UDP and DNS; the control through the proxy succeeds. Landlock is a second layer only.

SR-008.justification: Cage::with_options on T2 returns LowerError::Gaps with Construct::NetProxy; r36 on escape_linux.rs checks the same.

SR-009.justification: A run with a narrow list cannot use a concurrent wide run's listener (macOS refuses the connect; on T1 the address is the narrow run's own listener), its request is refused, the refusal is in the narrow run's record and the wide run's record holds none.

SR-010.justification: 64 KiB of pseudo-random bytes come back unchanged through CONNECT and SOCKS5; plain HTTP is forwarded byte for byte (plain_http_is_forwarded_only_for_the_host_it_names); the crate has no TLS code.

SR-011.justification: A stalled handshake is closed after the timeout, a connection beyond the limit is closed at once with Reason::Busy, and dropping the run closes an open relay.

SR-012.justification: A host with an escape sequence and a newline is recorded without control bytes; refusals enter the run's record through Record::push, which merges repeats and counts what exceeds the cap (crates/procage/src/violation.rs tests).

SR-013.justification: THREAT_MODEL lists R-35 (parser differential) and R-36 (direct egress) with canaries on both suites, the release status names shared hosting and fronting as residue, and site/content/docs/proxy.md says the allowlist binds host names, not content.
